record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Find all finite modular lattices for which every interval is self-dual. Do the same for finitary modular lattices with finite covers.

evidence.quote: [Stan2012, Ch. 3 Exer. 155(c)] Find all finite modular lattices for which every interval is self-dual. Do the same for finitary modular lattices with finite covers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice $L$ is a partially ordered set in which every pair of elements $x, y$ has a least upper bound (join) $x \vee y$ and a greatest lower bound (meet) $x \wedge y$. The lattice $L$ is called modular if for all $x, y, z \in L$ with $x \le z$ one has
$$ x \vee (y \wedge z) = (x \vee y) \wedge z. $$
For $a \le b$ in $L$, the interval $[a,b]$ is the sublattice $\{x \in L : a \le x \le b\}$. The dual of a lattice $(L, \le)$ is the lattice $(L, \ge)$ with the order reversed; $L$ is self-dual if it is isomorphic to its dual. A lattice is finitary if every interval $[a,b]$ is finite, and it has finite covers if every element covers and is covered by only finitely many elements.

(a) Classify all finite modular lattices $L$ with the property that every interval $[a,b] \subseteq L$ is self-dual.

(b) Classify all finitary modular lattices with finite covers having the same property: every interval is self-dual.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an exercise in Stanley's Enumerative Combinatorics Vol. 1 (Exercise 3.155(c)), and is listed in a contemporary notebook of open problems on tableau combinatorics, suggesting no full classification is known. Web searches did not surface a published complete classification of finite (or finitary with finite covers) modular lattices in which every interval is self-dual.
